title: No effect of a graded training program on the number of running-related injuries in novice runners: a randomized controlled trial
publisher: The American Journal of Sports Medicine
claims: The GRONORUN trial randomised 532 novice runners preparing for a recreational 4-mile (6.7 km) run to a graded 13-week programme based on the 10% rule or a standard 8-week programme.
A running-related injury was defined as any lower-extremity or back complaint that restricted running for at least one week.
Injury incidence was 20.8% in the graded group and 20.3% in the standard group (chi-square = 0.016, df = 1, P = .90).
The trial concluded that the graded 10%-rule programme had no effect on injury incidence compared with the shorter standard programme.
The introduction reports injury incidence ranges of 30% to 79% and 7 to 59 injuries per 1000 hours of running, and an estimate that 60% of running injuries can be attributed to training errors.

claimVerification.note: 原文：“Participants were novice runners (N = 532) preparing for a recreational 4-mile (6.7-km) running event”；“a standard 8-week training program (control group) and an adapted, graded, 13-week training program … based on the 10% training rule”。
原文：“An RRI was defined as any musculoskeletal complaint of the lower extremity or back causing a restriction of running for at least 1 week.”

原文结果：“The graded training program was not preventive for sustaining an RRI (χ2 = 0.016, df = 1, P = .90). The incidence of RRI was 20.8% in the graded training program group and 20.3% in the standard training program group.”数字、统计量完全一致。
原文结论：“no effect of a graded training program (13 weeks) in novice runners, applying the 10% rule, on the incidence of RRI compared with a standard 8-week training program.”
原文引言：“incidence rates of RRI vary from 30% to 79%, and from 7 to 59 RRIs per 1000 hours of running”；“It is estimated that 60% of all RRIs can be attributed to training errors”。三个数字与 claim 一致。
